coach.morning_action: Bois {{oz}} ounces maintenant. Reprends dans 25 minutes. Tu commences en déficit.
coach.morning_explanation: Perte nocturne : {{oz}} ounces. Réinitialise ta base avant l'entraînement.
coach.peak_action: Score {{score}}. Sommet. Bois 8 ounces avant la prochaine séance. Tiens la ligne.
coach.peak_explanation: Maintiens le rythme. Prends un stick si la chaleur ou l'effort augmente.
coach.balanced_action: Score {{score}}. Équilibré. Bois 12 ounces maintenant. Reprends dans 45 minutes.
coach.balanced_explanation: Tu es dans le rythme. Anticipe la prochaine chute.
coach.recovering_action: Score {{score}}. Récupération. Prends 1 stick avec 16 ounces maintenant. Reprends dans 20 minutes.
coach.recovering_explanation: Tu chutes. Inverse la courbe avant qu'elle s'accélère.
coach.depleted_action: Score {{score}}. Épuisé. Bois 20 ounces et prends 2 sticks maintenant. Reprends dans 10 minutes.
coach.depleted_explanation: Déficit critique. Électrolytes requis. La performance est compromise.
coach.social_drink_water_action: Bois 12 ounces d'eau maintenant. Espace ton prochain verre de 30 minutes.
coach.social_drink_water_explanation: S'hydrater après un verre protège demain. Un verre maintenant inverse la courbe.
coach.social_take_rtd_action: Prends 1 RTD maintenant. Bois 16 ounces d'eau avant la prochaine tournée.

coach.social_slow_intake_action: Bois de l'eau entre les verres. Tu en es à {{count}} — ralentis le rythme.
coach.social_slow_intake_explanation: Espacer les verres de 30+ minutes garde le score stable et la matinée claire.
coach.social_recovery_action: Bois 20 ounces d'eau et prends 1 RTD avant de dormir.
coach.social_recovery_explanation: Fenêtre de récupération ouverte. Deux unités de liquide + électrolytes maintenant font la différence.
coach.social_stop_explanation: Tu es dans une fenêtre d'affaiblissement élevé. Passe à l'eau et lance le protocole de récupération.
coach.social_do_not_drive_action: Ne conduis pas. Prends un VTC ou appelle un ami.
coach.social_do_not_drive_explanation: Tes réflexes et ton jugement sont réduits. Un trajet partagé est plus sûr.

v2.title: Sweat Calculator
v2.subhead: Measure your sweat rate, sodium loss, and the exact AForce replacement protocol — calibrated to ACSM and Baker 2017.
v2.heat_acclimatized_hint: ≥ 10 days of heat exposure / training in current climate
v2.helper_quick: Weigh nude or in dry clothing for accuracy. 1 lb of weight loss ≈ 16 ounces of sweat.
v2.helper_estimate: Estimate path uses your sport's population-mean sweat rate (Baker 2017) scaled by body surface area, intensity, and climate. Measure with a scale for the most accurate number.
v2.snap_hint: Run a calculation below for a calibrated reading.
v2.val_pre_weight: Enter a pre-weight between 1 and 700 lbs.
v2.val_post_weight: Enter a post-weight between 1 and 700 lbs.
v2.val_post_higher: Post-weight is higher than pre-weight — check your numbers.
v2.val_height: Height should be 0.5–8 ft (or leave blank).
v2.val_duration: Enter a duration between 1 and 600 minutes.
v2.val_need_weight: Enter your body weight to estimate without a scale.
v2.val_need_height: Set your height to estimate without a scale.
v2.perf_estimated_badge: ESTIMATED — measure with scale for precision
v2.perf_formula_note: AForce formula sodium: {{mg}}mg per serving — intentional by design
v2.ri_headline: Recovery is not driven by sodium alone.
v2.ri_body: AForce pairs {{mg}}mg of sodium with marine-sourced minerals and a pH 8.8 profile — designed to help you rehydrate, not flood you with salt.
v2.sys_ph_v: A smooth, higher-pH profile — part of the AForce standard.
v2.ing_seamoss_line: Marine source of 72 trace minerals critical to cellular function.
v2.ing_chlorella_line: Freshwater green algae — a whole-food source of chlorophyll and minerals.
v2.ing_dulse_line: Atlantic seaweed — a natural source of iodine and trace minerals.
v2.ai_sodium_line_one: Sodium loss {{loss}} mg → {{delivered}} mg delivered by {{sticks}} unit; gap {{gap}} mg covered by structured-water absorption.
v2.ai_sodium_line_other: Sodium loss {{loss}} mg → {{delivered}} mg delivered by {{sticks}} units; gap {{gap}} mg covered by structured-water absorption.
v2.opt_cooldown_hint: 15–20 min low HR before next bout.
v2.opt_salty_hint: Olives, broth, or pickle juice closes the sodium gap.
v2.opt_shower_hint: Drop core temp 1–2°F to free up cardiac output.
v2.opt_footer: For higher-output sessions, add a small pinch of Celtic sea salt if needed.
v2.gap_body: For sessions with high sodium loss add ¼ tsp of Celtic sea salt to your water between each AForce unit over the next 4 hours.
v2.gap_note: Celtic sea salt is minimally processed and retains a broad spectrum of naturally occurring trace minerals. It is philosophically aligned with AForce — unprocessed and ocean-sourced like our algae ingredients.
v2.cmp_closer: More sodium isn't always the goal — the right balance is.
v2.share_headline_gap: Sodium gap closed — smarter, not saltier.
v2.cite_formula_source: Source: Sawka MN et al. 2007. ACSM Position Stand. Med Sci Sports Exerc 39(2):377–390.
v2.cite_thresholds_body: >2% body weight loss → measurable performance decline; >4% → heat-illness risk.
v2.cite_thresholds_source: Sources: ACSM 2007 §C; Cheuvront SN, Kenefick RW. 2014. Compr Physiol 4(1):257–285.
v2.cite_ranges_body: Population mean ≈ 50 mmol/L (1150 mg/L); range 200–2300 mg/L.
v2.cite_ranges_source: Source: Baker LB. 2017. Sports Med 47(Suppl 1):111–128, Table 2.
v2.cite_strategy_body: Replace 100–150% of fluid loss within 4–6 h post-exercise; pair sodium intake with fluid for full re-equilibration.
v2.cite_strategy_source: Source: Sawka 2007 §G; Maughan RJ & Shirreffs SM. 2010. Scand J Med Sci Sports 20(s2):31–42.
v2.cite_estimate_body: Anchored to per-sport population-mean sweat rates (Baker 2017), scaled by Du Bois body-surface area, RPE-mapped intensity, USARIEM-style climate factors, and Périard 2015 acclimatization adjustment.
v2.cite_calibration: Calibration target: ±15% of measured rate at moderate intensity, thermoneutral conditions. Always confirm with a scale for clinical decisions. Not a medical device.
